---
title: "Data sources"
subtitle: "Every endpoint the project calls, what it yields, and what it costs"
---

Two channels, with different shapes and different cost models.

**Structured** (`session.py` → `document.py`): typed endpoints that answer in
fields. Batched by course list, cheap, and authoritative --- whatever comes back
here is never overwritten later.

**Unstructured** (`corpus.py`): prose and file bytes, stored verbatim. This is
where grading rules actually live, and no endpoint can be asked for them
directly.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  T["token"] --> S["MoodleSession"]
  S --> C1["Course set<br/><i>favourites, metadata</i>"]
  S --> C2["Activities<br/><i>4 module types</i>"]
  S --> C3["Personal state<br/><i>attempts, submissions</i>"]
  S --> C4["Prose & files<br/><i>8 endpoints + downloads</i>"]
  C1 --> D["CourseDocumentBuilder"]
  C2 --> D
  C3 --> D
  D --> DB[("moodle.sqlite")]
  C4 --> R["CorpusWriter"]
  R --> M[("corpus/ + manifest.json")]
```

## Course set

| Function | Yields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `core_webservice_get_site_info` | `userid`, `fullname`, `sitename`, `release`, `downloadfiles` | Also the token validity check |
| `core_course_get_enrolled_courses_by_timeline_classification` | Courses in one bucket | Called with `classification="favourites"` |
| `core_enrol_get_users_courses` | Every enrolment | Fallback path, and the enrichment source |
| `core_course_get_courses_by_field` | `contacts`, `overviewfiles` | The **only** source of lecturer names |

Scope is deliberately **favourites only** --- the courses you starred in Moodle.
A full enrolment list on a ZHAW account includes years of past modules; starring
is the cheapest signal of "this semester" that needs no heuristic.

`favourite_courses()` prefers the timeline endpoint (server-side filter) and
falls back to filtering `core_enrol_get_users_courses` on `isfavourite`
client-side. Both are covered by one `except (MoodleApiError, ValueError)` ---
`ValueError` is the allowlist refusing, `MoodleApiError` is the site not
exposing it, and the fallback answers either way.

The two endpoints disagree on field names, which `_normalise_course` reconciles:

```python
"category": course.get("coursecategory") or course.get("categoryname") or ""
```

Capability flags (`completion_enabled`, `activity_dates_shown`) are carried
through as tri-state. They matter because they let an empty deadline list stay
distinguishable from a feature the course has switched off.

## Activities

One call per module type, each taking the whole course list.

| Function | Record | Dates it carries |
|---|---|---|
| `mod_quiz_get_quizzes_by_courses` | `QuizRecord` | `timeopen`, `timeclose`, `timelimit` |
| `mod_assign_get_assignments` | `AssignRecord` | `allowsubmissionsfromdate`, `duedate`, `cutoffdate` |
| `mod_workshop_get_workshops_by_courses` | `WorkshopRecord` | 4 phase timestamps |
| `mod_lesson_get_lessons_by_courses` | `LessonRecord` | `available`, `deadline` |

Each type gets **its own record shape**. A shared one would force a lossy
choice at pull time, since a workshop carries four phase timestamps and an
assignment three distinct dates. What the shapes share is an identity block
(`type`, `course_id`, `cmid`, `instance`, `name`, `url`, `visible`), so records
of different types stay joinable.

Two normalisations happen here and nowhere else:

- **`0` is not a timestamp.** Moodle writes `0` into date fields it has no
  value for. Every timestamp passes through `ActivityRecord.timestamp()`, so
  "not set" arrives as `None` and a sort never places an unset deadline at the
  epoch.
- **`cmid` vs `instance`.** `cmid` is the course-module id (what a URL uses);
  `instance` is the per-module-type id (what `mod_quiz_*` status calls want).
  Both are kept, because confusing them is the most common way to get an empty
  result from a correct-looking call.

`mod_assign_get_assignments` nests assignments under courses while the other
three return a flat list, so it gets its own flattening loop rather than going
through `_records()`.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Blank records.** With `include_empty=True`, a course with no quizzes still
yields one all-`None` quiz record. This keeps "asked, genuinely none" distinct
from "never asked". `document.py` calls with `include_empty=False`, since the
document's own `[]` already carries that meaning.
:::

## Personal state

The only per-activity calls --- these do not batch, and they dominate the call
count.

| Function | Scope | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `mod_quiz_get_user_attempts` | one quiz | 1 call per quiz |
| `mod_quiz_get_user_best_grade` | one quiz | 1 call per quiz |
| `mod_assign_get_submission_status` | one assignment | 1 call per assignment |
| `core_completion_get_activities_completion_status` | one course | 1 call per course |

`QuizStatusRecord` filters previews out of the attempt list before counting, and
derives `is_outstanding` as *nothing finished and the window has not shut*.
`AssignStatusRecord` reads `lastattempt.submission` for status and timestamp,
`lastattempt.gradingstatus` for whether it has been marked, and collects
submitted filenames from the plugin file areas.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**`grade_achieved` is quiz-only.** `mod_quiz_get_user_best_grade` returns a
grade; nothing equivalent is pulled for assignments, workshops or lessons, so
`document.py` writes `None` for those with the comment *"needs the gradebook;
not pulled yet"*. The gradebook endpoint (`gradereport_user_get_grade_items`) is
**not** in the allowlist. Consequently no grade *scale* is known either --- only
raw points against `grade_max`, never a 1--6 mark or a letter.
:::

`session.completion()` is implemented and allowlisted but **is not called by
`CourseDocumentBuilder`**, so completion state never reaches the document. It
needs `core_course_get_contents` for activity names, because the completion
payload carries only `cmid`.

## Prose and files

Everything below is harvested verbatim into `corpus/`. Nothing is summarised,
converted or interpreted --- HTML stays HTML, bytes stay bytes. Interpretation is
[pass 1 and 2](extraction.qmd).

| Function | Yields | Stored as |
|---|---|---|
| `core_course_get_contents` | Sections, module intros, file inventory, URL modules | `section-summary`, `module-intro` |
| `mod_page_get_pages_by_courses` | Full page bodies | `page` |
| `mod_label_get_labels_by_courses` | Labels (inline course text) | `label` |
| `mod_book_get_books_by_courses` | Book intros | `book-intro` |
| `mod_url_get_urls_by_courses` | Outbound links | `links[]` in the manifest |
| `core_block_get_course_blocks` | Rendered sidebar blocks (`returncontents=True`) | `block` |
| `mod_forum_get_forums_by_courses` → `..._get_forum_discussions` → `..._get_discussion_posts` | Announcements and threads | `forum` |
| `mod_assign_get_assignments` | `introattachments` --- briefs attached to an assignment | downloaded file |
| `mod_lesson_get_pages` → `..._get_page_data` | Files embedded in lesson pages | downloaded file |

`core_course_get_contents` is the backbone: it returns both the structure and
most of the file inventory. The `mod_*_by_courses` calls exist because the
contents call returns a module's *name* but not always its *body*.

Two sources are off or costly by default (`HARVEST_INCLUDE_*` in `config.py`):
forums cost one call per forum plus one per discussion (on, since
announcements frequently carry a changed deadline); lesson files cost one call
per lesson page (off).

### Deduplication

Several endpoints return the same module. A label's `description` in
`core_course_get_contents` is its `intro` in `mod_label_get_labels_by_courses`;
a `url` module appears in both. Three keys prevent double-storing:

| Key | Prevents |
|---|---|
| `fileurl` | Downloading the same bytes twice |
| `(cmid, digest-of-body)` | Storing the same prose from two endpoints |
| `(cmid, url)` | Recording the same link twice |

Keyed by `cmid` rather than by text alone, so genuinely repeated boilerplate in
two *different* modules is still recorded twice --- which is the truth about the
course.

### Download limits

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_FILE_BYTES` | 128 MB | Refuse a single oversized file |
| `SKIP_MIMETYPE_PREFIXES` | `video/`, `audio/` | No text to extract |
| `DOWNLOAD_CHUNK` | 64 KB | A large file never sits in memory twice |
| `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` | 60 s | Per file, not per harvest |
| `MAX_NAME_LENGTH` | 60 | Longest path component written |

A skipped or failed file is still recorded in the manifest with a `skipped`
reason, so coverage gaps are visible rather than silent.

### Corpus layout

```
corpus/
  manifest.json                 provenance for every item
  screening.json                written by pass 1
  extraction.json               written by pass 2
  31803-ds-osi-hs26/
    text/0001_module-intro_gedrucktes-lehrbuch-vdf.html
    files/0008_osi-logistics-hs26-ds.pdf
```

The manifest is the index everything downstream reads. A `texts[]` entry:

```json
{
  "kind": "module-intro",
  "name": "Gedrucktes Lehrbuch (vdf)",
  "stored_path": "31803-ds-osi-hs26/text/0001_module-intro_gedrucktes-lehrbuch-vdf.html",
  "chars": 188,
  "section": "Vorlesungsunterlagen",
  "cmid": 2134191,
  "instance": 185248,
  "modname": "url",
  "module_name": "Gedrucktes Lehrbuch (vdf)",
  "module_url": "https://moodle.zhaw.ch/mod/url/view.php?id=2134191",
  "availability": null
}
```

A `files[]` entry adds `fileurl`, `mimetype`, `filesize`, `timemodified`,
`source`, and either `stored_path` + `bytes` or a `skipped` reason.
`stored_path` is the **stable id** for a document --- pass 1 and pass 2 both
address documents by it.

## Call cost

For *n* courses, *q* quizzes and *a* assignments:

| Stage | Calls |
|---|---|
| Structured sync | `~2` (course set) + `1` (by_field) + `4` (batched activities) + `2q` + `a` |
| Harvest | `~6` batched + `2n` (contents, blocks) + forums (`1` per forum + `1` per discussion) + one HTTP GET per file |

The real run: five courses carrying 20 quizzes and 1 assignment between them →
roughly 50 structured calls, against a harvest of 206 downloads totalling
210 MB. (Most activities in those courses exist only in prose, which is why the
document ends up with more assignments than the API ever returned.)

The asymmetry is the point. Deadlines are cheap and exact; the documents that
explain what they are worth are expensive and need a model to read. That split
is what the [extraction pipeline](extraction.qmd) is built around.
